subtitle: A larger league before the name changed

body: ISS Pro Evolution 2 is Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo's PlayStation football game, first released in Japan on 24 August 2000. It extends the previous game's on-field play and Master League, arriving in Europe in March 2001. The club competition now contains two divisions and twenty-four teams, giving promotion and the development of a squad a broader structure. It became the final entry in this branch to carry the ISS name before Pro Evolution Soccer. The familiar combination of immediate matches and a longer club project was already taking a recognisable form.

More clubs and the additional division give the Master League a longer path, making the team's results part of a competition that continues beyond one fixture. The player still has to create opportunities on the field through movement, passing and the timing of an attack. The sequel refines those interactions, giving an experienced player reasons to adjust the pace of familiar moves. Partial licensing introduces some real player names, while other presentation remains approximate. The central attraction is the football itself and the steady improvement of the group being taken into the next match.

The Japanese release included under-twenty-three national teams connected to the Sydney Olympic competition, material absent from the European edition. North America did not receive this release, following the earlier ESPN MLS GameNight variation instead. ISS Pro Evolution 2 won the sports-game award at the 2001 BAFTA Interactive Entertainment Awards. Its position at the end of the ISS Pro naming period makes it a bridge between the PlayStation series and the more widely recognised Pro Evolution Soccer identity, carrying forward a league mode and style of football that had already earned a dedicated audience.
